upstream.scope: Resident memory read from /proc/<pid>/statm instead of /proc/<pid>/stat field 24, exact from Linux 6.16, with PX-005's units and availability states unchanged; no kernel-version branch, no further memory field, no CPU, protocol, runtime or client change, no htop parity claim

entries.feature: Resident memory is /proc/<pid>/statm field 2 (resident) in pages times the scanned mount's own page size, never /proc/<pid>/stat field 24, with no kernel-version branch: exact from Linux 6.16 and the stable kernels carrying the same fix (6.15.7, 6.12.39, 6.6.99), and on every earlier kernel the same approximate counter field 24 reports (percpu_counters read without their per-CPU deltas from 6.2, per-thread caches added in after more than 64 page-fault events before it), so never worse; the metric definition and README state each regime, the bound of max(32, 2 x online CPUs) pages per online CPU per counter, a possible 0 B for a fresh process, and the cost of the extra read and of the pin

A statm that cannot be read after the record's stat was is handled with the existing states and never by falling back to stat field 24: refused is Denied and unreadable, oversized or anything but the kernel's line of seven plain counts is Unavailable, both on a record that is still published without degrading Completeness, while a process that ended between the two reads, confirmed by its stat being gone too when read again through the same directory, is counted as vanished and publishes nothing; a statm missing beside a stat that still reads is Unavailable, never an exit

Both files of a record are read through one handle on its /proc/<pid> directory, reached through the reader's own /proc/self/fd/<n> with std alone and opened only if it is a directory, so on a kernel procfs a PID reused between the two reads fails with ESRCH instead of lending another process's memory to the instance stat identified (a with_root tree that is not a kernel procfs gets the handle without that guarantee); a reader whose own /proc cannot name an open directory (every system but Linux, or a Linux reader without a usable /proc) reads by name without reporting it, and a record directory that may be searched but not read is skipped as Denied
entries.scope: PX-005-G01/Linux procfs roots and fixture trees/read-only; by name on other systems

entries.feature: A task with no address space, a kernel thread or a zombie, reads the kernel's statm of seven zeros and keeps the known 0 B PX-005 published for it from stat field 24

Correction to PX-005's record, which is not rewritten: its 'exact bytes' and SRUI-PX005-001's 'exact u64 byte count' describe integer storage and conversion, while the count converted, stat field 24, was the kernel's approximate get_mm_rss on every kernel since 6.2; stat, statm and status are 'the same inaccurate number' only before 6.16 and its stable backports; and SRUI-PX005-002's interface is superseded by statm field 2
